sanskrit: tato rāmo mahātejā vismayāt punar eva hi uvāca praṇato vākyam agastyam ṛṣisattamam
english: Then Rāma of great splendor, filled with wonder once again, bowed and spoke these words to Agastya, the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: bhagavan kiṃ tadā lokāḥ śūnyā āsan dvijottama dharṣaṇāṃ yatra na prāpto rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: "Revered one, O best of twice-born men, were the worlds then empty of any realm where Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, had not come to wreak his ravages?"

sanskrit: utāho hīnavīryās te babhuvuḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ bahiṣkṛtā varāstraiś ca bahavo nirjitā nṛpāḥ
english: "Or were those rulers of the earth lacking in valour? Were many kings excluded by superior weapons and overcome in battle?"

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā agastyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ uvāca rāmaṃ prahasan pitāmaha iveśvaram
english: Having heard the words of Rāghava, the venerable sage Agastya smiled and spoke to Rāma as the Grandfather Brahmā himself might address the Lord.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ bādhamānas tu pārthivān pārthivarṣabha cacāra rāvaṇo rāma pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate
english: "Thus oppressing kings in this fashion, O bull among kings, O lord of the earth, Rāvaṇa, O Rāma, ranged across the earth.

sanskrit: tato māhiṣmatīṃ nāma purīṃ svargapurīprabhām saṃprāpto yatra sāmnidhyaṃ paramaṃ vasuretasaḥ
english: Then he arrived at a city named Māhiṣmatī, radiant as the city of heaven, where the supreme presence of Vasuretās dwelt.

sanskrit: tulya āsīn nṛpas tasya pratāpād vasuretasaḥ arjuno nāma yasyāgniḥ śarakuṇḍe śayaḥ sadā
english: A king equal in might to Vasuretās himself ruled there — Arjuna by name — in whose quiver fire ever lay sleeping.

sanskrit: tam eva divasaṃ so 'tha haihayādhipatir balī arjuno narmadāṃ rantuṃ gataḥ strībhiḥ saheśvaraḥ
english: On that very day the mighty Arjuna, lord of the Haihayas, had gone to sport on the Narmadā river, accompanied by his wives, like a great lord.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo rākṣasendras tu tasyāmātyān apṛcchata kvārjuno vo nṛpaḥ so 'dya śīghram ākhyātum arhatha
english: Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, questioned his ministers: "Where is your king Arjuna today? You ought to tell me quickly."

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'ham anuprāpto yuddhepsur nṛvareṇa tu mamāgamanam avyagrair yuṣmābhiḥ saṃnivedyatām
english: "I am Rāvaṇa, come here desiring battle with that best of men. You must without delay inform him of my arrival."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ rāvaṇenoktās te 'mātyāḥ suvipaścitaḥ abruvan rākṣasapatim asāmnidhyaṃ mahīpateḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, those wise ministers replied to the lord of the rākṣasas that the king was not present.

sanskrit: śrutvā viśravasaḥ putraḥ paurāṇām arjunaṃ gatam apasṛtyāgato vindhyaṃ himavatsaṃnibhaṃ girim
english: Hearing from the citizens that Arjuna had gone elsewhere, the son of Viśravā turned away and came to the Vindhya mountain, which resembles the Himālaya.

sanskrit: sa tam abhram ivāviṣṭam udbhrāntam iva medinīm apaśyad rāvaṇo vindhyam ālikhantam ivāmbaram
english: Rāvaṇa beheld the Vindhya mountain — as if filling the sky, as if churning the earth, as if scratching the heavens with its peaks.

sanskrit: sahasraśikharopetaṃ siṃhādhyuṣitakandaram prapāta patitaiḥ śītaiḥ sāṭṭahāsam ivāmbubhiḥ
english: Adorned with a thousand peaks, its caverns haunted by lions, it seemed to burst into loud laughter as its cascading cold waterfalls fell.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvaiḥ sāpsarogaṇakiṃnaraiḥ sāha strībhiḥ krīḍamānaiḥ svargabhūtaṃ mahocchrayam
english: Where gods, dānavas, gandharvas, hosts of apsarases, kiṃnaras, and their women played together, it towered to a great height, become like heaven itself.

sanskrit: nadībhiḥ syandamānābhir agatipratimaṃ jalam sphuṭībhiś calajihvābhir vamantam iva viṣṭhitam
english: With rivers flowing freely through it, its waters seeming motionless like something at rest, with quivering-tongued lightning-flashes, it appeared to be vomiting forth its standing waters.

sanskrit: ulkāvantaṃ darīvantaṃ himavatsaṃnibhaṃ girim paśyamānas tato vindhyaṃ rāvaṇo narmadāṃ yayau
english: Gazing at the Vindhya mountain — flaring with meteors, riddled with caverns, resembling the Himālaya — Rāvaṇa then proceeded to the Narmadā.

sanskrit: calopalajalāṃ puṇyāṃ paścimodadhigāminīm mahiṣaiḥ sṛmaraiḥ siṃhaiḥ śārdūlarkṣagajottamaiḥ uṣṇābhitaptais tṛṣitaiḥ saṃkṣobhitajalāśayām
english: The holy Narmadā, flowing westward to the ocean, her waters stirred by rolling stones — her pools churned by buffaloes, spotted deer, lions, tigers, bears, and the finest elephants, all parched and thirsting under the heat.

sanskrit: cakravākaiḥ sakāraṇḍaiḥ sahaṃsajalakukkuṭaiḥ sārasaiś ca sadāmattaiḥ kokūjadbhiḥ samāvṛtām
english: Crowded with cakravāka birds and kāraṇḍava ducks, with swans and water-fowl, with sārasa cranes ever intoxicated with joy, and with the cries of kokila birds.

sanskrit: phulladrumakṛtottaṃsāṃ cakravākayugastanīm vistīrṇapulinaśroṇīṃ haṃsāvalisumekhalām
english: Adorned with blossoming trees as her crown, her bosom formed by pairs of cakravāka birds, her hips the broad sandbanks, her girdle the line of swans.

sanskrit: puṣpareṇvanuliptāṅgīṃ jalaphenāmalāṃśukām jalāvagāhasaṃsparśāṃ phullotpalaśubhekṣaṇām
english: Her body anointed with pollen of flowers, her garment the pure foam of her waters, pleasant to touch when wading into her current, her eyes the beautiful blossoming blue lotuses.

sanskrit: puṣpakād avaruhyāśu narmadāṃ saritāṃ varām iṣṭām iva varāṃ nārīm avagāhya daśānanaḥ
english: Quickly descending from the Puṣpaka chariot, the ten-headed one plunged into the Narmadā, best of rivers, as one plunges into a cherished and beautiful woman.

sanskrit: sa tasyāḥ puline ramye nānākusumaśobhite upopaviṣṭaḥ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ narmadā darśajaṃ harṣam āptavān rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: That foremost of rākṣasas, the lord of the rākṣasas, sat down on her beautiful sandbank adorned with many kinds of flowers, together with his ministers, and obtained the joy that comes from beholding the Narmadā.

sanskrit: tataḥ salīlaṃ prahasān rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ uvāca sacivāṃs tatra mārīcaśukasāraṇān
english: Then with a playful laugh, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, spoke there to his ministers Mārīca, Śuka, and Sāraṇa.

sanskrit: eṣa raśmisahasreṇa jagat kṛtveva kāñcanam tīkṣṇatāpakaraḥ sūryo nabhaso madhyam āsthitaḥ mām āsīnaṃ viditveha candrāyāti divākaraḥ
english: "The sun, with his thousand rays, having made the world as if golden, fierce in his heat, has taken his stand at the middle of the sky. Knowing that I am seated here, the day-maker now moves toward the moon."

sanskrit: narmadā jalaśītaś ca sugandhiḥ śramanāśanaḥ madbhayād anilo hy eṣa vāty asau susamāhitaḥ
english: "The wind that blows from the Narmadā is cool, fragrant, and dispels fatigue — it blows thus steadily out of fear of me."

sanskrit: iyaṃ cāpi saricchreṣṭhā narmadā narma vardhinī līnamīnavihaṃgormiḥ sabhayevāṅganā sthitā
english: "And this best of rivers, the Narmadā who augments delight, her waves holding fish and birds within them, stands like a woman filled with fear."

sanskrit: tad bhavantaḥ kṣatāḥ śastrair nṛpair indrasamair yudhi candanasya raseneva rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ
english: "Therefore you, wounded by the weapons of kings equal to Indra in battle, anointed with blood as if with sandal paste —"

sanskrit: te yūyam avagāhadhvaṃ narmadāṃ śarmadāṃ nṛṇām mahāpadmamukhā mattā gaṅgām iva mahāgajāḥ
english: "— you all shall plunge into the Narmadā, giver of happiness to men, like great bull-elephants with lotus-like faces, drunk with excitement, entering the Gaṅgā."

sanskrit: asyāṃ snātvā mahānadyāṃ pāpmānaṃ vipramokṣyatha
english: "Having bathed in this great river, you shall be released from sin."

sanskrit: aham apy atra puline śaradindusamaprabhe puṣpopaharaṃ śanakaiḥ kariṣyāmi umāpateḥ
english: "I too shall here, on this sandbank radiant as the autumn moon, slowly offer a floral offering to the lord of Umā."

sanskrit: rāvaṇenaivam uktās tu mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ samahodaradhūmrākṣā narmadām avagāhire
english: Thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, Mārīca, Śuka, Sāraṇa, Mahodara, and Dhūmrākṣa plunged into the Narmadā.

sanskrit: rākṣasendragajais tais tu kṣobhyate narmadā nadī vāmanāñjanapadmādyair gaṅgā iva mahāgajaiḥ
english: The river Narmadā was churned by those elephant-like lords among the rākṣasas, just as the Gaṅgā is churned by great elephants named Vāmana, Añjana, Padma, and others.

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasāḥ snātvā narmadāyā varāmbhasi uttīrya puṣpāṇy ājahrur balyarthaṃ rāvaṇasya tu
english: Then those rākṣasas, having bathed in the excellent waters of the Narmadā and emerged therefrom, gathered flowers for Rāvaṇa's offering.

sanskrit: narmadā puline ramye śubhrābhrasadṛśaprabhe rākṣasendrair muhūrtena kṛtaḥ puṣpamayo giriḥ
english: On the beautiful sandbank of the Narmadā, radiant as a white cloud, the lords of the rākṣasas piled up in a moment a mountain of flowers.

sanskrit: puṣpeṣūpahṛteṣv eva rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ avatīrṇo nadīṃ snātuṃ gaṅgātoyād ivāñjanaḥ
english: Even as the flowers were being brought, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, descended into the river to bathe, like the elephant Añjana descending into the waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: tatra snātvā ca vidhivaj japtvā japyam anuttamam narmadā salilāt tasmād uttatāra sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Having bathed there according to the prescribed rites and having muttered the most excellent of prayers, Rāvaṇa emerged from those waters of the Narmadā.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ prāñjaliṃ yāntam anvayuḥ saptarākṣasāḥ yatra yatra sa yāti sma rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ jāmbūnadamayaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra tatra sma nīyate
english: Seven rākṣasas followed Rāvaṇa as he proceeded with joined palms. Wherever Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, went, a liṅga made of gold was carried thither.

sanskrit: vālukavedimadhye tu tal liṅgaṃ sthāpya rāvaṇaḥ arcayām āsa gandhaiś ca puṣpaiś cāmṛtagandhibhiḥ
english: Rāvaṇa installed that liṅga in the midst of a sand altar and worshipped it with fragrant substances and with flowers that smelled like nectar.

sanskrit: tataḥ satām ārtiharaṃ haraṃ paraṃ varapradaṃ candramayūkhabhūṣaṇam samarcayitvā sa niśācaro jagau prasārya hastān praṇanarta cāyatān
english: Then, having worshipped Hara the supreme — remover of the distress of the good, the granter of boons, adorned with the rays of the moon — that night-wanderer sang aloud and danced, stretching his arms wide.

sanskrit: narmadā puline yatra rākṣasendraḥ sa rāvaṇaḥ puṣpopahāraṃ kurute tasmād deśād adūrataḥ
english: Not far from that spot on the Narmadā sandbank where Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, was making his floral offering —

sanskrit: arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ krīḍite saha nārībhir narmadātoyam āśritaḥ
english: — Arjuna, the foremost among the victorious, lord and master of Māhiṣmatī, was at play with his women in the waters of the Narmadā.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ madhyagato rāja rarāja sa tato 'rjunaḥ kareṇūnāṃ sahasrasya madhyastha iva kuñjaraḥ
english: King Arjuna, standing in the midst of those women, shone forth like a bull elephant standing in the midst of a thousand she-elephants.

sanskrit: jijñāsuḥ sa tu bāhūnāṃ sahasrasyottamaṃ balam rurodha narmadā vegaṃ bāhubhiḥ sa tadārjunaḥ
english: Wishing to test the supreme strength of his thousand arms, Arjuna at that time dammed the current of the Narmadā with those arms.

sanskrit: kārtavīryabhujāsetuṃ taj jalaṃ prāpya nirmalam kūlāpahāraṃ kurvāṇaṃ pratisrotaḥ pradhāvati
english: The pure water, meeting the dam of Kārtavīrya's arms, ran backward in reverse current, eroding the banks.

sanskrit: samīnanakramakaraḥ sapuṣpakuśasaṃstaraḥ sa narmadāmbhaso vegaḥ prāvṛṭkāla ivābabhau
english: Filled with fish, crocodiles, and tortoises, scattered with flowers and kuśa grass, that surge of the Narmadā's waters appeared like the onset of the rainy season.

sanskrit: sa vegaḥ kārtavīryeṇa saṃpreṣiṭa ivāmbhasaḥ puṣpopahāraṃ tat sarvaṃ rāvaṇasya jahāra ha
english: That surge of the water, as if dispatched by Kārtavīrya, swept away entirely all of Rāvaṇa's floral offering.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'rdhasamāptaṃ tu utsṛjya niyamaṃ tadā narmadāṃ paśyate kāntāṃ pratikūlāṃ yathā priyām
english: Rāvaṇa, abandoning the rite half-completed, then looked at the Narmadā as one looks at a beloved woman who has turned contrary.

sanskrit: paścimena tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā sāgarodgārasaṃnibham vardhantam ambhaso vegaṃ pūrvām āśāṃ praviśya tu
english: Seeing from the west the surge of the water growing, resembling the roaring of the ocean, then entering the eastern direction —

sanskrit: tato 'nudbhrāntaśakunāṃ svābhāvye parame sthitām nirvikārāṅganābhāsāṃ paśyate rāvaṇo nadīm
english: — Rāvaṇa then saw the river with her birds no longer startled, abiding in her natural supreme state, appearing like a woman without perturbation.

sanskrit: savyetarakarāṅgulyā saśabdaṃ ca daśānanaḥ vegaprabhavam anveṣṭuṃ so 'diśac chukasāraṇau
english: The ten-faced one, snapping his fingers on his right hand with a loud sound, dispatched Śuka and Sāraṇa to discover the source of the current.

sanskrit: tau tu rāvaṇasaṃdiṣṭau bhrātarau śukasāraṇau vyomāntaracarau vīrau prasthitau paścimonmukhau
english: Those two brothers Śuka and Sāraṇa, directed by Rāvaṇa, those two heroes who could travel through the sky, set out facing westward.

sanskrit: ardhayojanamātraṃ tu gatvā tau tu niśācarau paśyetāṃ puruṣaṃ toye krīḍantaṃ sahayoṣitam
english: Having traveled only half a yojana, those two night-wanderers saw a man at play in the water together with his women.

sanskrit: bṛhatsālapratīkaśaṃ toyavyākulamūrdhajam madaraktāntanayanaṃ madanākāravarcasaṃ
english: He was like a great sāla tree in form, his hair disheveled by the water, his eyes red at the corners from intoxication, his radiance like that of the god of love.

sanskrit: nadīṃ bāhusahasreṇa rundhantam arimardanam giriṃ pādasahasreṇa rundhantam iva medinīm
english: He was blocking the river with his thousand arms, that crusher of enemies, like a mountain blocking the earth with a thousand feet.

sanskrit: bālānāṃ varanārīṇāṃ sahasreṇābhisaṃvṛtam samadānāṃ kareṇūnāṃ sahasreṇeva kuñjaram
english: He was surrounded by a thousand young and beautiful women, like a bull elephant surrounded by a thousand she-elephants in full rut.

sanskrit: tam adbhutatamaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasau śukasāraṇau saṃnivṛttāv upāgamya rāvaṇaṃ tam athocatuḥ
english: Having seen that most wondrous being, the two rākṣasas Śuka and Sāraṇa turned back, approached Rāvaṇa, and spoke to him.

sanskrit: bṛhatsālapratīkāśaḥ ko 'py asau rākṣaseśvara narmadāṃ rodhavad ruddhvā krīḍāpayati yoṣitaḥ
english: "Who is that being, O lord of the rākṣasas, resembling a great sāla tree, who, having dammed the Narmadā completely, makes the women play?"

sanskrit: tena bāhusahasreṇa saṃniruddhajalā nadī sāgarodgārasaṃkāśān udgārān sṛjate muhuḥ
english: "The river, her waters blocked by those thousand arms, repeatedly sends forth surges resembling the roaring of the ocean."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bhāṣamāṇau tau niśamya śukasāraṇau rāvaṇo 'rjuna ity uktvā uttasthau yuddhalālasaḥ
english: Hearing those two Śuka and Sāraṇa speaking thus, Rāvaṇa exclaimed "It is Arjuna!" and rose up, eager for battle.

sanskrit: arjunābhimukhe tasmin prasthite rākṣaseśvare sakṛd eva kṛto rāvaḥ saraktaḥ preṣito ghanaiḥ
english: As that lord of the rākṣasas set out facing toward Arjuna, a single thunderous roar with a crimson hue was sent forth by the clouds.

sanskrit: mahodaramahāpārśvadhūmrākṣaśukasāraṇaiḥ saṃvṛto rākṣasendras tu tatrāgād yatra so 'rjunaḥ
english: Surrounded by Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, Dhūmrākṣa, Śuka, and Sāraṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas came to where that Arjuna was.

sanskrit: nātidīrgheṇa kālena sa tato rākṣaso balī taṃ narmadā hradaṃ bhīmam ājagāmāñjanaprabhaḥ
english: In no great length of time that mighty rākṣasa, dark as the elephant Añjana, arrived at that terrible pool of the Narmadā.

sanskrit: sa tatra strīparivṛtaṃ vāśitābhir iva dvipam narendraṃ paśyate rājā rākṣasānāṃ tadārjunam
english: There the king of the rākṣasas saw Arjuna, that lord of men, surrounded by women just as a bull elephant is surrounded by she-elephants in rut.

sanskrit: sa roṣād raktanayano rākṣasendro baloddhataḥ ity evam arjunāmātyān āha gambhīrayā girā
english: The lord of the rākṣasas, his eyes red with rage, swollen with pride in his strength, spoke these words to the ministers of Arjuna in a deep voice.

sanskrit: amātyāḥ kṣipram ākhyāta haihayasya nṛpasya vai yuddhārthaṃ samanuprāpto rāvaṇo nāma nāmataḥ
english: "Ministers, quickly inform the king of the Haihayas that one named Rāvaṇa has arrived seeking battle."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mantriṇo 'thārjunasya te uttasthuḥ sāyudhās taṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ vākyam abruvan
english: Hearing Rāvaṇa's words, the ministers of Arjuna rose up armed and spoke these words to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: yuddhasya kālo vijñātaḥ sādhu bhoḥ sādhu rāvaṇa yaḥ kṣībaṃ strīvṛtaṃ caiva yoddhum icchasi no nṛpam vāśitāmadhyagaṃ mattaṃ śārdūla iva kuñjaram
english: "Well and good, well and good, O Rāvaṇa, your understanding of the right time for battle! You who wish to fight our king when he is intoxicated and surrounded by women — like a tiger wishing to fight a maddened elephant in the midst of she-elephants."

sanskrit: kṣamasvādya daśagrīva uṣyatāṃ rajanī tvayā yuddhaśraddhā tu yady asti śvas tāta samare 'rjunam
english: "Forgive us today, O ten-necked one, let the night be spent by you here; if you have determination for battle, then tomorrow, good sir, fight Arjuna in the field."

sanskrit: yadi vāpi tvarā tubhyaṃ yuddhatṛṣṇāsamāvṛtā nihatyāsmāṃs tato yuddham arjunenopayāsyasi
english: "Or if you are seized with urgent thirst for battle, then slay us first, and after that you shall engage Arjuna in combat."

sanskrit: tatas te rāvaṇāmātyair amātyāḥ pārthivasya tu sūditāś cāpi te yuddhe bhakṣitāś ca bubhukṣitaiḥ
english: Then those ministers of the king were struck down in battle by the ministers of Rāvaṇa, and were devoured by the famished ones.

sanskrit: tato halahalāśabdo narmadā tira ābabhau arjunasyānuyātrāṇāṃ rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇām
english: Then a tumultuous uproar arose along the bank of the Narmadā from the retinue of Arjuna and the ministers of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: iṣubhis tomaraiḥ śūlair vajrakalpaiḥ sakarṣaṇaiḥ sarāvaṇān ardayantaḥ samantāt samabhidrutāḥ
english: With arrows, javelin-spears, lances, and thunderbolt-like weapons along with plowshare-clubs, they charged from all sides, afflicting all of Rāvaṇa's host.

sanskrit: haihayādhipayodhānāṃ vega āsīt sudāruṇaḥ sanakramīnamakarasamudrasyeva nisvanaḥ
english: The onslaught of the warriors of the Haihaya lord was terrifyingly fierce, like the sound of an ocean filled with fish, crocodiles, and great sea-monsters.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya tu te 'mātyāḥ prahastaśukasāraṇāḥ kārtavīryabalaṃ kruddhā nirdahanty agnitejasaḥ
english: But the ministers of Rāvaṇa — Prahasta, Śuka, and Sāraṇa — blazing with the energy of fire, enraged, burned through the army of Kārtavīrya.

sanskrit: arjunāya tu tat karma rāvaṇasya samantriṇaḥ krīḍamānāya kathitaṃ puruṣair dvārarakṣibhiḥ
english: The deed of Rāvaṇa with his ministers was reported to Arjuna, who was still at play, by the men guarding the gates.

sanskrit: uktvā na bhetavyam iti strījanaṃ sa tato 'rjunaḥ uttatāra jalāt tasmād gaṅgātoyād ivāñjanaḥ
english: Telling the women "Do not be afraid," Arjuna then emerged from those waters, like the elephant Añjana emerging from the waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: krodhadūṣitanetras tu sa tato 'rjuna pāvakaḥ prajajvāla mahāghoro yugānta iva pāvakaḥ
english: His eyes inflamed by anger, Arjuna then blazed up like fire, most terrifying, like the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: sa tūrṇataram ādāya varahemāṅgado gadām abhidravati rakṣāṃsi tamāṃsīva divākaraḥ
english: Swiftly taking up his mace adorned with excellent golden armlets, he rushed upon the rākṣasas as the sun rushes upon darkness.

sanskrit: bāhuvikṣepakaraṇāṃ samudyamya mahāgadām gāruḍaṃ vegam āsthāya āpapātaiva so 'rjunaḥ
english: Lifting high the great mace for a sweeping arm-blow, and assuming the speed of Garuḍa, Arjuna swooped down.

sanskrit: tasya margaṃ samāvṛtya vindhyo 'rkasyeva parvataḥ sthito vindhya ivākampyaḥ prahasto musalāyudhaḥ
english: Blocking his path as the Vindhya mountain blocks the path of the sun, Prahasta stood immovable as the Vindhya itself, armed with his club.

sanskrit: tato 'sya musalaṃ ghoraṃ lohabaddhaṃ madoddhataḥ prahastaḥ preṣayan kruddho rarāsa ca yathāmbudaḥ
english: Then Prahasta, swollen with pride and enraged, hurling his terrible iron-bound club, roared like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: tasyāgre musalasyāgnir aśokāpīḍasaṃnibhaḥ prahastakaramuktasya babhūva pradahann iva
english: At the tip of that club, as it left Prahasta's hand, fire appeared like a garland of aśoka blossoms, as if burning everything.

sanskrit: ādhāvamānaṃ musalaṃ kārtavīryas tadārjunaḥ nipuṇaṃ vañcayām āsa sagado gajavikramaḥ
english: Kārtavīrya Arjuna, of the valour of an elephant and armed with his mace, skillfully dodged that charging club.

sanskrit: tatas tam abhidudrāva prahastaṃ haihayādhipaḥ bhrāmayāṇo gadāṃ gurvīṃ pañcabāhuśatocchrayām
english: Then the lord of the Haihayas charged at Prahasta, whirling his heavy mace, as tall as five hundred arms.

sanskrit: tenāhato 'tivegena prahasto gadayā tadā nipapāta sthitaḥ śailo vajrivajrahato yathā
english: Struck by it with extreme force, Prahasta fell where he stood, like a mountain struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: prahastaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mārīcaśukasāraṇāḥ samahodaradhūmrākṣā apasṛptā raṇājirāt
english: Seeing Prahasta fallen, Mārīca, Śuka, Sāraṇa, Mahodara, and Dhūmrākṣa withdrew from the battlefield.

sanskrit: apakrānteṣv amātyeṣu prahaste ca nipātite rāvaṇo 'bhyadravat tūrṇam arjunaṃ nṛpasattamam
english: With his ministers retreated and Prahasta felled, Rāvaṇa quickly rushed upon Arjuna, that best of kings.

sanskrit: sahasrabāhos tad yuddhaṃ viṃśadbāhoś ca dāruṇam nṛparākṣasayos tatra ārabdhaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: The dreadful battle between the thousand-armed and the twenty-armed, between the king and the rākṣasa, began there — hair-raising to witness.

sanskrit: sāgarāv iva saṃkṣubdhau calamūlāv ivācalau tejoyuktāv ivādityau pradahantāv ivānalau
english: Like two agitated oceans, like two mountains with quaking roots, like two suns blazing with energy, like two fires burning everything.

sanskrit: baloddhatau yathā nāgau vāśitārthe yathā vṛṣau meghāv iva vinardantau siṃhāv iva balotkaṭau
english: Like two elephants maddened by pride, like two bulls fighting over a cow in heat, like two thunderclouds roaring, like two lions supremely powerful.

sanskrit: rudrakālāv iva kruddhau tau tathā rākṣasārjunau parasparaṃ gadābhyāṃ tau tāḍayām āsatur bhṛśam
english: Like two wrathful Rudras at the time of dissolution, the rākṣasa and Arjuna struck each other again and again fiercely with their maces.

sanskrit: vajraprahārān acalā yathā ghorān viṣehire gadāprahārāṃs tadvat tau sahete nararākṣasau
english: As mountains endure the terrible blows of Indra's thunderbolt, so those two, man and rākṣasa, endured the blows of each other's maces.

sanskrit: yathāśaniravebhyas tu jāyate vai pratiśrutiḥ tathā tābhyāṃ gadāpātair diśaḥ sarvāḥ pratiśrutāḥ
english: As an echo arises from thunderclaps among the clouds, so all directions resounded with the fall of their maces.

sanskrit: arjunasya gadā sā tu pātyamānāhitorasi kāñcanābhaṃ nabhaś cakre vidyutsaudāmanī yathā
english: The mace of Arjuna, falling upon the enemy's chest, made the sky shine like gold, like the lightning of a storm-cloud.

sanskrit: tathaiva rāvaṇenāpi pātyamānā muhur muhuḥ arjunorasi nirbhāti gadolkeva mahāgirau
english: Likewise the mace wielded by Rāvaṇa, falling again and again upon Arjuna's chest, shone like a blazing meteor upon a great mountain.

sanskrit: nārjunaḥ khedam āpnoti na rākṣasagaṇeśvaraḥ samam āsīt tayor yuddhaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ balīndrayoḥ
english: Neither Arjuna grew weary nor the lord of the rākṣasa hosts; their battle was equal, as the battle of Bali and Indra once was.

sanskrit: śṛṅgair maharṣabhau yadvad dantāgrair iva kuñjarau parasparaṃ vinighnantau nararākṣasasattamau
english: Like two great bulls striking each other with their horns, like two elephants striking each other with the tips of their tusks, those foremost of man and rākṣasa struck each other mutually.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunena kruddhena sarvaprāṇena sā gadā stanayor antare muktā rāvaṇasya mahāhave
english: Then by the enraged Arjuna, with all his might, the mace was released in the great battle against the space between Rāvaṇa's breasts.

sanskrit: varadānakṛtatrāṇe sā gadā rāvaṇorasi durbaleva yathā senā dvidhābhūtāpatat kṣitau
english: On Rāvaṇa's chest, protected by the boon he had received, that mace broke in two as it fell to the ground, like a weak army.

sanskrit: sa tv arjunapramuktena gadāpātena rāvaṇaḥ apāsarpad dhanurmātraṃ niṣasāda ca niṣṭanan
english: Rāvaṇa, struck by the mace hurled by Arjuna, stumbled back the distance of a bowshot and sat down, groaning.

sanskrit: sa vihvalaṃ tad ālakṣya daśagrīvaṃ tato 'rjunaḥ sahasā pratijagrāha garutmān iva pannagam
english: Perceiving the ten-necked one to be overcome, Arjuna suddenly seized him as Garuḍa seizes a serpent.

sanskrit: sa taṃ bāhusahasreṇa balād gṛhya daśānanam babandha balavān rājā baliṃ nārāyaṇo yathā
english: That powerful king, seizing the ten-faced one with force by his thousand arms, bound him, as Nārāyaṇa bound Bali.

sanskrit: badhyamāne daśagrīve siddhacāraṇadevatāḥ sādhvīti vādinaḥ puṣpaiḥ kiranty arjunamūrdhani
english: As the ten-necked one was being bound, siddhas, cāraṇas, and gods, exclaiming "Well done!", showered flowers upon Arjuna's head.

sanskrit: vyāghro mṛgam ivādāya siṃharāḍ iva dantinam rarāsa haihayo rājā harṣād ambudavan muhuḥ
english: The Haihaya king, like a tiger carrying off a deer, like the lord of lions carrying an elephant, roared repeatedly with joy like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: prahastas tu samāśvasto dṛṣṭvā baddhaṃ daśānanam saha tai rākasaiḥ kruddha abhidudrāva pārthivam
english: But Prahasta, having recovered, seeing the ten-faced one bound, enraged, charged at the king together with those rākṣasas.

sanskrit: naktaṃcarāṇāṃ vegas tu teṣām āpatatāṃ babhau uddhṛta ātapāpāye samudrāṇām ivādbhutaḥ
english: The onslaught of those night-wanderers as they charged was like the wondrous swelling of the oceans when summer's heat has passed.

sanskrit: muñca muñceti bhāṣantas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cāsakṛt musalāni ca śūlāni utsasarjus tadārjune
english: Shouting "Release him! Release him!" and repeatedly "Stand fast! Stand fast!", they hurled clubs and lances at Arjuna.

sanskrit: aprāptāny eva tāny āśu asaṃbhrāntas tadārjunaḥ āyudhāny amarārīṇāṃ jagrāha ripusūdanaḥ
english: Even before those weapons reached him, Arjuna, unagitated, that destroyer of enemies, swiftly caught all the weapons of those foes of the immortals.

sanskrit: tatas tair eva rakṣāṃsi durdharaiḥ pravarāyudhaiḥ bhittvā vidrāvayām āsa vāyur ambudharān iva
english: Then with those very irresistible and superior weapons, he shattered and scattered the rākṣasas as the wind scatters clouds.

sanskrit: rākṣasāṃs trāsayitvā tu kārtavīryārjunas tadā rāvaṇaṃ gṛhya nagaraṃ praviveśa suhṛdvṛtaḥ
english: Having terrified the rākṣasas, Kārtavīrya Arjuna then, taking Rāvaṇa captive, entered his city surrounded by his friends.

sanskrit: sa kīryamāṇaḥ kusumākṣatotkarair dvijaiḥ sapauraiḥ puruhūtasaṃnibhaḥ tadārjunaḥ saṃpraviveśa tāṃ purīṃ baliṃ nigṛhyaiva sahasralocanaḥ
english: Showered with heaps of flowers and unhusked grain by the twice-born and the citizens, Arjuna, resembling Puruhūta — like thousand-eyed Indra — then entered that city, having indeed subdued Bali.

sanskrit: rāvaṇagrahaṇaṃ tat tu vāyugrahaṇasaṃnibham ṛṣiḥ pulastyaḥ śuśrāva kathitaṃ divi daivataiḥ
english: The sage Pulastya heard of the capture of Rāvaṇa — a capture like the seizing of the wind — as it was being narrated by the gods in heaven.

sanskrit: tataḥ putrasutasnehāt kampyamāno mahādhṛtiḥ māhiṣmatīpatiṃ draṣṭum ājagāma mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: Then, moved by affection for his son's son and of great steadfastness, the great sage came to see the lord of Māhiṣmatī.

sanskrit: sa vāyumārgam āsthāya vāyutulyagatir dvijaḥ purīṃ māhiṣmatīṃ prāpto manaḥsaṃtāpavikramaḥ
english: That twice-born one, taking the path of the wind, moving with a speed equal to the wind, driven by the anguish of his mind, arrived at the city of Māhiṣmatī.

sanskrit: so 'marāvatisaṃkāśāṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām praviveśa purīṃ brahmā indrasyevāmarāvatīm
english: He entered that city resembling Amarāvatī, filled with joyful and prosperous people, as Brahmā might enter Indra's Amarāvatī.

sanskrit: pādacāram ivādityaṃ niṣpatantaṃ sudurdṛśam tatas te pratyabhijñāya arjunāya nyavedayan
english: Recognizing him as he came on foot, dazzling to look upon like the sun at its rising, they announced him to Arjuna.

sanskrit: pulastya iti taṃ śrutvā vacanaṃ haihayādhipaḥ śirasy añjalim uddhṛtya pratyudgacchad dvijottamam
english: Hearing that word "Pulastya," the lord of the Haihayas raised his joined palms to his head and went forward to meet that best of twice-born men.

sanskrit: purohito 'sya gṛhyārghyaṃ madhuparkaṃ tathaiva ca purastāt prayayau rājña indrasyeva bṛhaspatiḥ
english: His purohita, taking the ceremonial water-offering and the honey-mixture, proceeded in front of the king, as Bṛhaspati before Indra.

sanskrit: tatas tam ṛṣim āyāntam udyantam iva bhāskaram arjuno dṛśya saṃprāptaṃ vavandendra iveśvaram
english: Then seeing that sage arriving like the rising sun, Arjuna, beholding his coming, bowed as Indra bows before the Lord.

sanskrit: sa tasya madhuparkaṃ ca pādyam arghyaṃ ca dāpayan pulastyam āha rājendro harṣagadgadayā girā
english: Causing to be offered to him the honey-mixture, water for the feet, and the arghya gift, that lord of kings spoke to Pulastya with a voice choked with joy.

sanskrit: adyeyam amarāvatyā tulyā māhiṣmatī kṛtā adyāhaṃ tu dvijendrendra yasmāt paśyāmi durdṛśam
english: "Today Māhiṣmatī has been made equal to Amarāvatī; today am I indeed blessed, O lord among twice-born, O Indra among sages, because I behold what is so hard to behold."

sanskrit: adya me kuśalaṃ deva adya me kulam uddhṛtam yat te devagaṇair vandyau vande 'haṃ caraṇāv imau
english: "Today is my well-being assured, O divine one; today is my lineage exalted — for I bow to those feet of yours which the hosts of gods themselves bow before."

sanskrit: idaṃ rājyam ime putrā ime dārā ime vayam brahman kiṃ kurma kiṃ kāryam ājñāpayatu no bhavān
english: "This kingdom, these sons, these wives, we ourselves — O Brahman, what shall we do? What is to be done? Let your honor command us."

sanskrit: taṃ dharme 'gniṣu bhṛtyeṣu śivaṃ pṛṣṭvātha pārthivam pulastyovāca rājānaṃ haihayānāṃ tadārjunam
english: Having then auspiciously inquired of that king about his welfare in matters of dharma, sacred fires, and servants, Pulastya spoke to Arjuna, that king of the Haihayas.

sanskrit: rājendrāmalapadmākṣapūrṇacandranibhānana atulaṃ te balaṃ yena daśagrīvas tvayā jitaḥ
english: "O king of kings, you of spotless lotus eyes, of a face resembling the full moon — unequalled is your strength, by which the ten-necked one has been conquered by you."

sanskrit: bhayād yasyāvatiṣṭhetāṃ niṣpandau sāgarānilau so 'yam adya tvayā baddhaḥ pautro me 'tīvadurjayaḥ
english: "He of whom the ocean and the wind stand motionless out of fear — that same grandson of mine, most exceedingly difficult to conquer, has today been bound by you."

sanskrit: tat putraka yaśaḥ sphītaṃ nāma viśrāvitaṃ tvayā madvākyād yācyamāno 'dya muñca vatsa daśānanam
english: "Therefore, my son, your fame and name have been made renowned by you — now being besought at my word, dear child, release the ten-faced one today."

sanskrit: pulastyājñāṃ sa gṛhyātha akiṃcanavaco 'rjunaḥ mumoca pārthivendrendro rākṣasendraṃ prahṛṣṭavat
english: Receiving the command of Pulastya without hesitation, that Indra among the lords of the earth, Arjuna, gladly released the lord of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa taṃ pramuktvā tridaśārim arjunaḥ prapūjya divyābharaṇasragambaraiḥ ahiṃsākaṃ sakhyam upetya sāgnikaṃ praṇamya sa brahmasutaṃ gṛhaṃ yayau
english: Having released that enemy of the thirty gods, Arjuna honored him with divine ornaments, garlands, and garments, entered into a non-aggression friendship with him with fire as witness, bowed to that son of Brahmā, and went home.

sanskrit: pulastyenāpi saṃgamya rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān pariṣvaṅgakṛtātithyo lajjamāno visarjitaḥ
english: The mighty lord of the rākṣasas too, having met with Pulastya, was dismissed by him with an embrace as his act of hospitality, Rāvaṇa feeling ashamed.

sanskrit: pitāmahasutaś cāpi pulastyo munisattamaḥ mocayitvā daśagrīvaṃ brahmalokaṃ jagāma saḥ
english: And Pulastya, that best of sages, son of the Grandfather Brahmā, having caused the ten-necked one to be freed, went to Brahmaloka.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ prāptaḥ kārtavīryāt tu dharṣaṇāt pulastyavacanāc cāpi punar mokṣam avāptavān
english: Thus did Rāvaṇa, having been subjected to humiliation by Kārtavīrya, again obtain his release through the words of Pulastya.

sanskrit: evaṃ balibhyo balinaḥ santi rāghavanandana nāvajñā parataḥ kāryā ya icchec chreya ātmanaḥ
english: "Thus, O joy of the Raghu line, there are those more powerful than the powerful. One who desires his own welfare should never show contempt for another."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā piśitāśanānāṃ sahasrabāhor upalabhya maitrīm punar narāṇāṃ kadanaṃ cakāra cacāra sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ ca darpāt
english: Then that king of the flesh-eaters, having obtained the friendship of the thousand-armed one, once again wrought slaughter among men and roamed the entire earth with pride.
